To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is no evidence of a systematic or consistent approach to the prosecution of parents for non-attendance at school.
the prosecution of mothers is a disproportionate response to a problem of truancy that is rooted in social inequality.
the prosecution of a parent under section 444 is a disproportionate response to truancy and is unfair on single mothers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the way in which the criminal justice system is being used to enforce the law on truancy.
the way in which the law and the courts have interpreted and applied the power to prosecute under section 444.
the ways in which parents, and in particular mothers, are constructed as ‘bad’ or ‘deviant’ by the criminal justice system, and the implications this may have for their children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the law is unfair to single parent mothers, and that the law is also unfair to children.
the prosecution of single parent mothers under s.444 is unfair and that the law and its application is discriminatory.
there is a strong prima facie case for the repeal of the power to prosecute under section 444.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prosecution of single mothers is a form of social control, and that the law and its application are gendered in nature.
the law is a blunt tool that has been used in a discriminatory and unfair way.
the law is unfair and that there are a number of reasons for this.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the law and policy concerned with the prosecution of parents has been used to target mothers, in particular, those who are single parent mothers.
the law is being used to criminalise parents who are already disadvantaged by their socio-economic status.
the prosecution of single parent mothers is a gendered and class-based form of social control that has the potential to exacerbate rather than ameliorate problems of truancy.
